PakDataKit's datasets live in `data/` and are generated by
`scripts/generate-data.mjs` (except `networks.json`, `area-codes.json`,
`holidays.json` and `sales-tax-rates.json`, which are edited directly). Two official lists are kept as
extracted CSV files in `data/sources/` and read by the generator: Pakistan
Post's post code directory and the 2023 census's administrative units. The exported `dataVersion` is the
date the data was last checked.

The datasets were audited against official sources on 16 November 2026;
[AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md) has the findings, the fixes made and what is still open.

Official bodies (PTA, NADRA, SBP, Pakistan Post) publish few machine-readable
lists, so some entries rest on secondary sources. Each section says how sure we
are. To correct an entry, open an issue or pull request with a source.

## Banks (`banks.json`): IBAN bank codes

- **Dataset:** `banks.json` (id `banks`), 50 records. Scheduled banks, microfinance banks and EMIs in Pakistan: 50 IBAN codes, 47 websites, 16 SWIFT/BIC codes.
- **Source:** State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), SBP lists of regulated institutions (names, types, websites); IBANs printed by SBP (codes); SWIFT/BIC codes only as printed by SBP or on each institution's own domain, each with its URL (https://www.sbp.org.pk/sbp-regulated-institutions/commercial-banks), undated; retrieved 2026-11-23, checked 2026-11-23.
- **Applies:** 2026-11-16 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-02-16 (quarterly, and after any SBP merger or licence notification).

SBP does not publish a list of IBAN bank codes, and IBAN codes do not always
match SWIFT BIC prefixes (e.g. Silkbank is `SAUD`). Codes are therefore checked
against real IBANs. Names follow SBP's lists of regulated institutions
(https://www.sbp.org.pk/sbp-regulated-institutions/commercial-banks and
.../microfinance-banks, retrieved 2026-11-16), with a former name kept in
brackets where people still search for it.

- **Confirmed from IBANs printed by SBP:** 35 codes, from SBP's list of dam
  fund accounts at every bank
  (https://archive.sbp.org.pk/notifications/FD/DamFund/Detail-1.pdf, undated,
  about 2018, retrieved 2026-11-16): `AIIN`, `ABPA`, `ASCM`, `ALFH`, `BAHL`,
  `BKIP`, `KHYB`, `BPUN`, `BKCH`, `CITI`, `DEUT`, `DUIB`, `FAYS`, `FWOM`,
  `HABB`, `MPBL`, `ICBK`, `JSBL`, `MUCB`, `MCIB`, `MEZN`, `NBPA`, `SAMB`,
  `SAUD`, `SIND`, `SMES`, `SONE`, `SCBL`, `SUMB`, `UNIL`, `ZTBL` (Zarai
  Taraqiati Bank), `TMFB`, `WMBL`, `FMFB` and `SMFB` (Sindh Microfinance
  Bank). The same list shows an `SBPP` IBAN in use. `ZTBL` and `SMFB` were
  added on 2026-11-16 from this list. (It prints ICBC's IBAN with a digit `1`
  for the `I`; the checksum is only valid with `ICBK`.)
- **Also confirmed from IBANs printed by SBP:** `KHBL` (Khushhali), `JCMA`
  (Mobilink Microfinance Bank), `FINC` (ABHI, as FINCA), `UMBL`, `NRSP` and
  `APNA`, from SBP's account lists for the Prime Minister's Flood Relief Fund
  2022 (https://archive.sbp.org.pk/IBANs-of-PM-Flood-Relief-Fund.pdf) and the
  2023 relief fund for Türkiye and Syria
  (https://archive.sbp.org.pk/ReliefFund-Turkiye.pdf), both retrieved
  2026-11-16. That makes 41 codes confirmed by SBP documents.
- **Confirmed from published IBANs on smaller sites:** `SADA` (SadaPay), `NAYA`
  (NayaPay).
- **Confirmed from real account IBANs shared by a maintainer:** `RQMI` (Raqami
  Islamic Digital Bank) and `MSHQ` (Mashreq Bank Pakistan), both digital banks.
- **Legacy codes with no official source:** `MCBL`, `NBPB`, `TAMW` and `NIBP`.
- **Not included, because no code could be confirmed:** Punjab Provincial
  Cooperative Bank, LOLC Microfinance Bank (formerly Pak Oman), Halan
  Microfinance Bank (formerly Advans), ASA Microfinance Bank, the EMIs Finja,
  Akhtar Fuiou Technologies, E-Processing Systems, Wemsol and YAP Pakistan,
  HugoBank, KT Bank and Bank of AJK. A second search on 2026-11-16 (SBP's
  relief-fund lists and each institution's own website) found no printed IBAN
  for any of them.
- **Types** follow SBP's groups on its list of regulated institutions:
  "Public Sector Commercial Banks" are `public-sector` (National Bank of
  Pakistan, Sindh Bank, The Bank of Khyber, The Bank of Punjab), "Local
  Private Banks" are `commercial`, and "Islamic", "Foreign", "Specialized"
  and "Digital" banks have the type of the same name.
- **Spelling.** Names use each bank's own styling ("Bank Alfalah Limited",
  "Bank Al Habib Limited", "BankIslami Pakistan Limited", "Citibank N.A.
  Pakistan"). SBP's list spells some differently, and not consistently
  ("Bank Al-Falah Limited", "Bank Al-Habib Limited", "Al-Baraka Bank
  (Pakistan) Limited", "Bank Islami Pakistan Limited", "Citi Bank N.A",
  "Industrial & Commercial Bank of China", "Allied Bank limited"), so it is
  recorded here and not copied.
- **Closed:** `SMES` → "SME Bank Limited (in liquidation)", `active: false`.
  SBP cancelled its licence and de-scheduled it on 17 March 2025
  (https://archive.sbp.org.pk/notifications/bprd/2025/ntf6.htm). `NIBP` was
  de-scheduled on 7 July 2017 on its merger into MCB Bank
  (https://archive.sbp.org.pk/notifications/bprd/2017/ntf2.htm).
- **Merged or renamed** banks keep their code with the current name, e.g.
  `SAUD` → "Silkbank Limited (merged into United Bank Limited)" (de-scheduled
  by SBP on 10 March 2025,
  https://archive.sbp.org.pk/notifications/bprd/2025/ntf4.htm) and `TMFB` →
  "Easypaisa Bank Limited" (a scheduled bank from 23 January 2025,
  https://archive.sbp.org.pk/notifications/bprd/2025/ntf1.htm).

### Websites and SWIFT/BIC codes (2.8.0)

Kept in `data/sources/bank-details.json` and merged into `banks.json` by
`scripts/generate-data.mjs`. All checked 2026-11-23.

- **Websites (47):** from SBP's lists of regulated institutions
  (https://www.sbp.org.pk/sbp-regulated-institutions/commercial-banks and
  .../microfinance-banks). Where the bank now uses another domain, `website`
  is the bank's current one and `websiteSbpListed` keeps SBP's: Askari
  (`askaribank.com.pk`), ABHI (`finca.pk`), Mobilink (`waseelabank.com`) and
  Standard Chartered (`standardchartered.com.pk`). Bank Alfalah's SBP link is
  an Outlook "safelinks" redirect; the plain URL is used. Deutsche Bank and
  Mashreq point to the Pakistan page of the group site. Bank of China, ICBC,
  NayaPay and SadaPay have no website in SBP's lists; theirs come from their
  own sites. NIBP and SAUD (merged) and SMES (in liquidation) have none, with
  `status` and `mergedInto` naming the successor where there is one.
- **SWIFT/BIC (16 codes, 15 banks):** only codes printed by SBP or on the
  institution's own domain, stored as the 8-character BIC, with the printed
  form, URL, page and date (`swiftSource`). Not used: codes derived from
  SBP's list of Roshan Digital Account codes or from branch codes, NBP's
  code in an S&P Global profile hosted on its site, aggregator sites, and
  BankIslami's 10-character "BKIPPKKXXX". SWIFT's own directory search is
  behind a CAPTCHA and was not used.
- **1LINK IMD codes:** not included. There is no official public source;
  1LINK shares them with members only (its members page returns 404, and
  SBP's pages do not list them).

No SWIFT/BIC code, and why:

- `AIIN` (Al Baraka Bank (Pakistan) Limited): No page on the bank's own domain prints a BIC.
- `ALFH` (Bank Alfalah Limited): Only the Roshan Digital Account branch code ALFHPKKARDA is printed (SBP list, bank pages); the 8-character code would be derived.
- `APNA` (Apna Microfinance Bank): Microfinance bank; no BIC printed on its own domain (it may have none).
- `BKIP` (BankIslami Pakistan Limited): The bank's site prints "BKIPPKKXXX", which has 10 characters and is not a valid BIC.
- `BPUN` (The Bank of Punjab): The bank's trade pages are behind an Imperva security check; not bypassed. Only branch codes appear in search results.
- `DUIB` (Dubai Islamic Bank Pakistan Limited): Only the Roshan Digital Account branch code DUIBPKKARDA is printed (SBP list, dibpak.com).
- `FAYS` (Faysal Bank Limited): The bank's document that prints it is behind a Cloudflare challenge; not bypassed.
- `FINC` (ABHI Microfinance Bank (formerly FINCA Microfinance Bank)): Microfinance bank; no BIC printed on its own domain (it may have none).
- `FMFB` (HBL Microfinance Bank (formerly First MicroFinance Bank)): Microfinance bank; no BIC printed on its own domain (it may have none).
- `FWOM` (First Women Bank Limited): No page on the bank's own domain prints a BIC.
- `JCMA` (Mobilink Microfinance Bank (JazzCash)): Microfinance bank; no BIC printed on its own domain (it may have none).
- `KHBL` (Khushhali Microfinance Bank): Microfinance bank; no BIC printed on its own domain (it may have none).
- `KHYB` (The Bank of Khyber): Only a branch code is printed ("khybpkka 024"); the page that may print it returns "Access denied".
- `MPBL` (Habib Metropolitan Bank Limited): Only the Roshan Digital Account branch code MPBLPKKARDA is printed (SBP list); no habibmetro.com page prints the code.
- `MSHQ` (Mashreq Bank Pakistan Limited): No Mashreq Pakistan page prints a BIC.
- `NAYA` (NayaPay): Electronic money institution, not a bank; no BIC printed.
- `NBPA` (National Bank of Pakistan): Only printed in an S&P Global profile hosted on nbp.com.pk, not an NBP document; NBP's own documents print only the branch code NBPAPKKAMBR.
- `NBPB` (National Bank of Pakistan): Only printed in an S&P Global profile hosted on nbp.com.pk, not an NBP document; NBP's own documents print only the branch code NBPAPKKAMBR.
- `NIBP` (NIB Bank Limited (merged into MCB Bank)): Merged into MCB Bank.
- `NRSP` (NRSP Microfinance Bank): Microfinance bank; no BIC printed on its own domain (it may have none).
- `RQMI` (Raqami Islamic Digital Bank Limited): No page on the bank's own domain prints a BIC.
- `SADA` (SadaPay): Electronic money institution, not a bank; no BIC printed.
- `SAMB` (Samba Bank Limited): Only the Roshan Digital Account branch code SAMBPKKARDA is printed (SBP list); the bank FAQ that printed it is gone.
- `SAUD` (Silkbank Limited (merged into United Bank Limited)): Merged into United Bank Limited.
- `SIND` (Sindh Bank Limited): No page on the bank's own domain prints a BIC (its IBFT page shows only the short code SND).
- `SMES` (SME Bank Limited (in liquidation)): In liquidation.
- `SMFB` (Sindh Microfinance Bank): Microfinance bank; no BIC printed on its own domain (it may have none).
- `SONE` (Soneri Bank Limited): Only branch codes are printed (SONEPKKACTO, SONEPKKALHR, SONEPKKASIK); the 8-character code would be derived.
- `SUMB` (Bank Makramah Limited (formerly Summit Bank)): No page on the bank's own domain prints a BIC.
- `TAMW` (Easypaisa Bank Limited (formerly Tameer Microfinance Bank)): No page on the bank's own domain prints a BIC.
- `TMFB` (Easypaisa Bank Limited (formerly Telenor Microfinance Bank)): No page on the bank's own domain prints a BIC.
- `UMBL` (U Microfinance Bank): Microfinance bank; its site calls the 4-letter IBAN code "UMBL" a SWIFT code, which it is not.
- `WMBL` (Mobilink Microfinance Bank (JazzCash)): Microfinance bank; no BIC printed on its own domain (it may have none).
- `ZTBL` (Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited): No page on the bank's own domain prints a BIC.

## Mobile networks (`networks.json`)

- **Dataset:** `networks.json` (id `networks`), 53 records. Every 03XX mobile prefix and the operator it was allocated to.
- **Source:** Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), PTA National Numbering Plan 2008 (https://www.pta.gov.pk/assets/media/nnp_08_final.pdf), dated 2008; retrieved 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-16.
- **Applies:** 2008 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-02-16 (quarterly).

`03XX` prefixes and the operator each was originally allocated to. PTA has no
current operator-by-prefix table. Its National Numbering Plan 2008 paper
(https://www.pta.gov.pk/assets/media/nnp_08_final.pdf, retrieved 2026-11-16)
gives the two-digit allocations: 30 Mobilink (Jazz), 31 Paktel (now Zong), 32
Warid (now Jazz), 33 Ufone, 34 Telenor, 35 SCO, 36 Instaphone, and 37 to 39
"for future use". Individual prefixes are cross-checked with Google
libphonenumber and operator announcements.

- `0329` (Jazz) and `0355` (SCO) included.
- `0370`–`0371` (Zong) included, from libphonenumber only. **Unverified:**
  two searches in November 2026 (PTA's annual reports for 2021 to 2024, its
  numbering documents and licensee list, the ITU page for Pakistan and
  zong.com.pk) found no official document that gives 037x to an operator. `0372`–`0379` are **not**
  included, as no allocation or use was found.
- `0364` (Instaphone, licence cancelled in 2008) is not included.
- `034x` is labelled Telenor, the original allocation. Telenor Pakistan was
  merged into PTML (Ufone) in July 2026: PTCL announced the "successful
  completion of the amalgamation" on 2 July 2026
  (https://ptcl.com.pk/Home/PressReleaseDetail/?ItemId=934&linkId=130,
  retrieved 2026-11-16). The label is kept because the dataset records the
  operator a prefix was allocated to, no new brand has been announced
  officially (PTCL still writes "Ufone 5G"), and PTA's own pages still list
  Telenor Pakistan. With number portability, the current operator can differ
  for any prefix.

## Landline area codes (`area-codes.json`)

- **Dataset:** `area-codes.json` (id `area-codes`), 114 records. Fixed-line area codes in every province and territory.
- **Source:** Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), Pakistan's national numbering plan as communicated by PTA to the ITU (https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-t/oth/02/02/T02020000A10002PDFE.pdf), dated 2021-11-09; retrieved 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-16.
- **Applies:** 2021-11-09 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-11-16 (when PTA files a new numbering plan with the ITU; checked yearly).

114 codes, from the numbering plan PTA sent to the ITU on 9 November 2021
(https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-t/oth/02/02/T02020000A10002PDFE.pdf,
retrieved 2026-11-16), which lists every code with its district. The 73 codes
held before November 2026 came from PTCL's national dialling-code list
(https://ptcl.com.pk/Info/National-Dialing-Codes) and all appear in the ITU
plan with the same districts.

- **Added 2026-11-16 from the ITU plan:** 18 codes in Balochistan (`822`
  Zhob to `856` Awaran), 8 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (`924` Khyber and Mohmand,
  `932` Malakand, `939` Buner, `942` Bajaur, `944` Upper Dir, `945` Lower
  Dir, `965` South Waziristan, `996` Shangla), 7 in Gilgit-Baltistan (`5811`
  Gilgit to `5817` Astore) and 8 in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (`5821` Neelum to
  `5828` Bhimber).
- Names are the districts the plan gives, spelt as in `districts.json` so
  that `getAreaCode` finds them: the plan writes "Neelum", "Sudonthi",
  "Bhimer" and "K.Abdullah / Pishin" for Neelam, Sudhnuti, Bhimber and Killa
  Abdullah and Pishin. `832` is listed there as Bolan, the former name of
  Kachhi district; both names find it. For the two districts split since
  2021, the successors are listed with the plan's name: `835` Dera Bugti,
  North Dera Bugti and South Dera Bugti; `965` South Waziristan, Lower South
  Waziristan and Upper South Waziristan.
- PTCL's own list differs for Azad Jammu and Kashmir (Muzaffarabad "58",
  Kotli "574") and has no Mirpur or Gilgit entry. The ITU plan is the newer
  list from PTA, so it is followed.
- **Non-geographic numbers** (since 2.7.0), from PTA's documents only:
  - **UAN**: an area code, then `111` and six digits, 11 to 13 digits in all
    ("National Universal Access Number" in the ITU plan of 9 November 2021,
    page 1). Written without the area code (`111-123-456`), as UANs are
    advertised, it is accepted with `e164: null`.
  - **Toll-free**: `0800` and five or six digits. The ITU plan gives five
    ("National Toll Free Number", same page: `800 XXXXX`, 8 digits in all).
    PTA's National Numbering Plan 2008 gives six: "the numbers take the form
    of '0800' access code + 6-digit virtual number (e.g. 0800 544321)"
    (section 8.1) and the structure table "(0)800 XXXXXX" (section 8.1.4),
    in both its final version and version 4
    (https://www.pta.gov.pk/assets/media/num_plan_230108.pdf, section 8.1.4,
    retrieved 2026-11-22). Six-digit numbers are in use: Soneri Bank
    publishes `0800005000` (https://soneribank.com/complaint-and-suggestions,
    retrieved 2026-11-22). Both lengths are accepted since 2.7.1; 2.7.0
    accepted only five. An 8-digit form taken from libphonenumber was
    accepted before 2.7.0; no PTA document lists it, so it stays rejected.
  - **Premium rate**: `0900` and five digits. The 2021 plan does not list
    0900; PTA's National Numbering Plan 2008 (Consultation Paper, final
    version, 25 June 2008, section 9.1.4,
    https://www.pta.gov.pk/assets/media/nnp_08_final.pdf, retrieved
    2026-11-22) gives this as the "current structure". The 6-digit form in
    the same paper was a proposal.
  - **Personal (`0122`)**: seen in use, no PTA source, not supported
    (decided 2026-11-22). libphonenumber lists `0122` as personal numbers,
    but neither PTA's 2021 plan nor its 2008 paper does, so since 2.7.0
    `analyzeNumber` returns `null` for them and `validateLandline` rejects
    them with or without `services`. The `personal` number type is kept so
    existing code compiles, is never returned, and will be removed in 3.0.
  - For UANs the 2008 paper gives `111` and seven digits; the 2021 plan,
    which is newer and was sent to the ITU, gives an area code, `111` and
    six digits, and is followed. (2.7.0's notes called the paper's six-digit
    toll-free form a proposal too; that was wrong: section 8.1 states it as
    the form of 0800 numbers, and 2.7.1 accepts it.)
- **Number lengths** are not taken from the ITU plan (its length table could
  not be read reliably). The patterns in `numbers.ts` come from
  libphonenumber's PK metadata (v9.0.41), which already accepted numbers in
  all 41 added codes: ten digits in all for the `58xx` codes, so a four-digit
  code is followed by six digits.

## Districts (`districts.json`)

- **Dataset:** `districts.json` (id `districts`), 177 records. 177 districts as of October 2026, all provinces and territories.
- **Source:** Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS); provincial governments, 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 by province; later provincial notifications (https://www.pbs.gov.pk/wp-content/uploads/census_tables/tables/table_1_punjab_province.pdf), undated; retrieved 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-16.
- **Applies:** 2026-10-01 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-02-16 (quarterly, and after a provincial notification creates a district).

177 districts as of October 2026: Punjab 41, Sindh 30, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 40,
Balochistan 41, Gilgit-Baltistan 14, Azad Jammu and Kashmir 10, Islamabad 1.

> **Unverified: Central Dir, Allai and Paharpur** (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa). They
> rest on a news report of January 2026, not on a notification. Official
> pages updated in November 2026 do not show them: Malakand Division lists
> 10 districts without Central Dir (cmd.kp.gov.pk), Hazara Division lists 8
> without Allai (chd.kp.gov.pk), and the KP Bureau of Statistics'
> Development Statistics 2026 has Allai as a tehsil of Batagram and Paharpur
> as a tehsil of Dera Ismail Khan (all retrieved 2026-11-16). They are kept
> until a notification settles it either way. Nine more districts are also
> not confirmed on an official page; see the end of this section.

- **Khyber Pakhtunkhwa** (APP, January 2026: "increased to 40"): Lower and Upper
  South Waziristan (2022), Central Dir and Allai (January 2023), Paharpur
  (November 2025), Bar Swat (January 2026; reported as "Upper Swat" before
  the Board of Revenue notification of 27 January 2026).
- **Balochistan** (Revenue Department notification, 8 July 2026; Dawn,
  ProPakistani): Quetta split into Quetta East and Quetta West; Dera Bugti
  became South Dera Bugti and Upper Dera Bugti became North Dera Bugti; new
  Barshore, Tump and Wadh districts; Hub and Usta Muhammad (2022). Taftan is not
  included: no notification was found and the official count of 41 is reached
  without it.
- **Punjab:** Taunsa, Kot Addu, Murree, Wazirabad and Talagang (2022). A 2026
  notification of four more districts was confirmed fake.
- **Sindh:** proposed Karachi district renames (2024) were not found notified,
  so current names are kept.
- Former names (Quetta, Dera Bugti, Upper Dera Bugti, South Waziristan, Upper
  Swat) still resolve in `getDistrictProvince`.
- **Official confirmation, checked 2026-11-16** (details in AUDIT.md,
  section 9). Confirmed on official pages: Murree, Talagang, Wazirabad, Kot
  Addu and Taunsa (Punjab Board of Revenue list); Lower and Upper South
  Waziristan and Hub (Election Commission delimitation report, 2023); Bar
  Swat (Malakand Division's website); Usta Muhammad, Barshore and Tump
  (Balochistan budget documents, June 2026). **Not confirmed on any official
  page that could be read:** Central Dir, Allai and Paharpur (Khyber
  Pakhtunkhwa's divisional websites and its Development Statistics 2026
  still show Allai and Paharpur as tehsils and list no Central Dir); Quetta
  East and West, North and South Dera Bugti and Wadh (Balochistan); and
  Darel, Tangir, Gupis-Yasin and Roundu (Gilgit-Baltistan's 2024-25
  development programme treats them as sub-divisions). These stay in the
  dataset on the strength of the notifications and reports cited above, and
  are the entries most likely to need correcting.

## Cities (`cities.json`)

- **Dataset:** `cities.json` (id `cities`), 226 records. District headquarters, major towns and every city with a postal code.
- **Source:** Pakistan Post; Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), Derived: district headquarters and every city in Pakistan Post's post code directory (https://www.pakpost.gov.pk/images/national%20post%20code%20directory.pdf), dated 2021-02; retrieved 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-16.
- **Applies:** 2026-11-16 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-02-16 (regenerated with the postal and district data).

District headquarters and major towns, plus every city that has a postal code
in `postal-codes.json`, each mapped to its province.

## Postal codes (`postal-codes.json`, `post-offices.json`)

- **Dataset:** `postal-codes.json` (id `postal-codes`), 457 records. Postal codes with their delivery area, city and province.
- **Source:** Pakistan Post, Post Code Directory of Delivery Post Offices, Part I (https://www.pakpost.gov.pk/images/national%20post%20code%20directory.pdf), dated 2021-02; retrieved 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-16.
- **Applies:** 2021-02 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-02-16 (quarterly; Pakistan Post rarely republishes the directory).
- **Dataset:** `post-offices.json` (id `post-offices`), 2,560 records. Delivery post offices in every province.
- **Source:** Pakistan Post, Post Code Directory of Delivery Post Offices, Part I (https://www.pakpost.gov.pk/images/national%20post%20code%20directory.pdf), dated 2021-02; retrieved 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-16.
- **Applies:** 2021-02 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-02-16 (quarterly; Pakistan Post rarely republishes the directory).

Both files come from Pakistan Post's "Post Code Directory of Delivery Post
Offices" (Part I), a 45-page PDF dated February 2021
(https://www.pakpost.gov.pk/images/national%20post%20code%20directory.pdf,
retrieved 2026-11-16). Its office name, code, account office and province
columns are extracted to `data/sources/pakpost-delivery-post-offices.csv`
(2,564 rows), and `scripts/generate-data.mjs` builds both files from it.

- **`post-offices.json`** (2,560 entries, for `getPostOffice` and
  `searchPostOffices`): every office, as `code`, `office` (the directory's
  name in title case), `town`, `district` and `province`. The directory
  lists four codes twice, for the same place under two spellings (`22190`,
  `40520`, `56320`, `63050`); the first row is kept.
- **`postal-codes.json`** (457 entries, for `getCityByPostalCode`,
  `getPostalCode`, `getPostalCodes`, `getPostalAreas` and
  `searchPostalCodes`): only the offices that belong to a city in
  `cities.json`, as `city`, `postalCode`, `area` (the office name),
  `province`, and `district` and `primary` where they apply.
- **Which city an office belongs to.** The directory has no city column, so
  this is worked out:
  1. the 110 entries checked by hand before the import keep their city
     (including the eight codes corrected in November 2026);
  2. an office named after a city in `cities.json`, in the same province,
     belongs to that city ("ABBOTTABAD GPO" → Abbottabad);
  3. every office under the Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad account offices
     belongs to that city;
  4. an office whose name starts or ends with the city of its own account
     office belongs to that city ("GULISTAN COLONY, FAISALABAD").

  Any other office is in a town or village that is not on the city list. It
  is only in `post-offices.json`, where `town` is the office's own name
  ("Dulmial"); `getCityByPostalCode` returns `null` for it.

- **District** is given only where the town is the headquarters a district
  is named after (349 offices). An account office can serve several
  districts, so it is not used to guess one.
- **Province** is the directory's, with its spelling normalised ("Azad
  Kashmir" → Azad Jammu and Kashmir, "Federal Capital" → Islamabad Capital
  Territory, and the misprints "Punjba" and "SIndh").
- **Primary.** `getPostalCode(city)` returns the hand-checked code for the 95
  cities that had one. For 63 more cities it returns the code of the office
  named "<city> GPO", or else the office named after the city.
- **Names** are converted from the directory's capitals to title case; its
  spellings are kept, including misprints ("Islamabad Primr Minister
  Sectt.").
- **Not included:** the 740 or so non-delivery post offices of Part II
  (https://www.pakpost.gov.pk/images/LIST%20OF%20NON%20DELIVERY%20POs.pdf).
- The directory is dated 2021. Pakistan Post's web table
  (https://www.pakpost.gov.pk/postcodes.php) is missing many offices, so it
  is not the source; it was used for the spot-check below.

## Divisions and tehsils (`divisions.json`, `tehsils.json`)

- **Dataset:** `divisions.json` (id `divisions`), 30 records. 30 divisions at the 2023 census.
- **Source:** Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 by province (https://www.pbs.gov.pk/wp-content/uploads/census_tables/tables/table_1_punjab_province.pdf), undated; retrieved 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-16.
- **Applies:** 2023-03-01 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-11-16 (yearly, or after a provincial notification creates a division).
- **Dataset:** `tehsils.json` (id `tehsils`), 591 records. 591 tehsil-level units at the 2023 census, with their current district.
- **Source:** Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 by district (https://www.pbs.gov.pk/wp-content/uploads/census_tables/tables/table_1_punjab_districts.pdf), undated; retrieved 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-16.
- **Applies:** 2023-03-01 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-02-16 (quarterly, with the district data).

From Table 1 of the 2023 census (Pakistan Bureau of Statistics), which lists
every administrative unit with its area and population. Retrieved 2026-11-16:

- tehsils by district:
  https://www.pbs.gov.pk/wp-content/uploads/census_tables/tables/table_1_punjab_districts.pdf
  and the same file name for `sindh`, `kp` and `balochistan`, plus
  `table_1_islamabad.pdf`;
- districts by division: `table_1_punjab_province.pdf` and the same for the
  other three provinces.

The rows are extracted to `data/sources/census-2023-admin-units.csv`. The
totals match the census report's Table 1.1: **30 divisions, 136 districts and
591 tehsil-level units** (Punjab 146, Sindh 138, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 148,
Balochistan 158, Islamabad 1).

- **Tehsil-level units** are what the census counts: 306 tehsils, 107
  talukas (Sindh), 134 sub-divisions (Karachi, the merged districts of Khyber
  Pakhtunkhwa and much of Balochistan), 43 sub-tehsils (Balochistan) and one
  de-excluded area (Rajanpur). Each entry has a `type`.
- **Census district.** Every tehsil has a `censusDistrict`: the district it
  was in at the census. The census had 136 districts; `districts.json` has
  the 177 of today. Three census districts have since been split and are no
  longer district names: Quetta, Dera Bugti and South Waziristan.
- **Current district.** `currentDistrict` is the same as `censusDistrict`
  for the 119 census districts that have not lost territory to a new
  district. For tehsils of the 17 that have (Rawalpindi, Chakwal,
  Gujranwala, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, South Waziristan, Upper Dir,
  Batagram, Dera Ismail Khan, Swat, Lasbela, Jaffarabad, Quetta, Dera Bugti,
  Pishin, Kech and Khuzdar) it is set only where an official
  source confirms where the tehsil is now, and is `null` otherwise.
  - **Confirmed (Punjab, all 25 tehsils of the five parent districts):**
    Murree and Kotli Sattian are in Murree district; Talagang and Lawa in
    Talagang; Wazirabad in Wazirabad; Kot Addu and Chowk Sarwar Shaheed in
    Kot Addu; Taunsa and Koh-e-Suleman in Taunsa; the others stay in
    Rawalpindi, Chakwal, Gujranwala, Muzaffargarh and Dera Ghazi Khan.
    Source: the Board of Revenue's list of tehsils by district as on 31
    December 2023, in the Punjab Bureau of Statistics' Statistical Pocket
    Book 2025
    (https://bos.punjab.gov.pk/system/files/Statistical%20Pocket%20Book%202025%20Final.pdf,
    retrieved 2026-11-16). That list also has tehsils created since the
    census (Vehova, Alipur Chatha and others), which are not in this data.
  - **Not confirmed, so `null` (78 tehsils):** the tehsils of Swat, Upper
    Dir, Batagram, Dera Ismail Khan and South Waziristan (Khyber
    Pakhtunkhwa) and of Quetta, Dera Bugti, Pishin, Kech, Khuzdar, Lasbela
    and Jaffarabad (Balochistan). No official list of tehsils by district
    for today's districts could be read for either province.
- **Divisions** are the census's 30. Divisions created since (Gujrat in
  Punjab, listed on punjab.gov.pk) are not included, and districts created
  since the census have no division here.
- **Not covered:** Azad Jammu and Kashmir (3 divisions, 10 districts, 32
  tehsils per "AJK at a Glance 2023") and Gilgit-Baltistan. The census tables
  have no rows for them, and no official list of their tehsils was found.
- **Spelling** is the census's, in title case, with district names changed
  to ours ("UMER KOT" → Umerkot, "KAMBAR SHAHDAD KOT" → Qambar Shahdadkot,
  "TORGHAR" → Tor Ghar).
- **Repaired by hand.** The letters "LLA" are missing from four names in the
  district tables' text (the PDF prints them, but they do not come out of
  it). They are restored in `data/sources/census-2023-admin-units.csv`:

  | Census text    | Restored to     | Evidence                                                 |
  | -------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `AI`           | Allai           | Allai tehsil of Batagram; KP Development Statistics 2026 |
  | `KAR KAHAR`    | Kallar Kahar    | Punjab Board of Revenue tehsil list ("Kalar Kahar")      |
  | `KAR SAYADDAN` | Kallar Sayaddan | Punjab Board of Revenue tehsil list ("Kallar Syedan")    |
  | `TANDO AHYAR`  | Tando Allahyar  | The census's own province table prints "TANDO ALLAHYAR"  |

## Public holidays (`holidays.json`)

- **Dataset:** `holidays.json` (id `holidays`), 7 records. Calendar years 2020-2026 as observed; later Islamic holidays estimated.
- **Source:** Cabinet Division; State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), Cabinet Division holiday notifications and SBP circular letters; each date has its own source URL (https://cabinet.gov.pk), undated; retrieved 2026-11-16, checked 2026-11-16.
- **Applies:** 2020-01-01 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2026-12-15 (each December, when the Cabinet Division issues next year's holidays).

Eid ul Fitr, Eid ul Adha, Ashura and Eid Milad un Nabi dates actually observed
in 2020–2026; each entry has a `source` URL, and every source is a Cabinet
Division notification or an SBP circular letter (checked 2026-11-16; the last
seven news links, for 2020–2023, were replaced that day with the SBP circular
that states the same dates). Later years are estimated from the tabular Hijri calendar
and marked `estimated: true`. Fixed-date holidays follow the years they applied
in (e.g. Iqbal Day restored in 2022, Youm-e-Takbeer from 2024).

## Sales tax rates (`sales-tax-rates.json`)

- **Dataset:** `sales-tax-rates.json` (id `sales-tax-rates`), 9 records. Standard rates on goods (federal) and services (each province and ICT) from 1 July 2019.
- **Source:** FBR; Punjab Revenue Authority; Sindh Revenue Board; KP Revenue Authority; Balochistan Revenue Authority, Sales Tax Act 1990, s. 3(1); provincial sales tax on services Acts; each period has its own law and source (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20267171373418951SalesTaxAct1990updatedupto30.06.2026.pdf), dated 2026-06-30; retrieved 2026-11-18, checked 2026-11-18.
- **Applies:** 2019-07-01 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-07-15 (after the federal and provincial Finance Acts each July).

Standard rates only, from 1 July 2019, each with the period it applied, the
law that sets it and an official document. Edited directly. Reduced, higher
and sector rates (telecom at 19.5%, restaurants paid by card, Third Schedule
goods, further tax and so on) are not included. All documents retrieved
2026-11-18.

| Tax                                         | Rate | Applied               | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Goods, federal (FBR)                        | 17%  | to 22 February 2023   | Sales Tax Act 1990, s. 3(1); the Finance (Supplementary) Act 2023 replaces "seventeen" with "eighteen" (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20232231921422957Finance(Supplementary)Act,2023.pdf)                                                                                                               |
| Goods, federal (FBR)                        | 18%  | from 23 February 2023 | The same Act, in force at once on 23 February 2023; FBR Circular 01/2023; still 18% in FBR's Sales Tax Act "updated up to 30.06.2026" (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20267171373418951SalesTaxAct1990updatedupto30.06.2026.pdf)                                                                          |
| Services, Punjab (PRA)                      | 16%  | whole period          | Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012, s. 2(41A) ("Standard Rate" means sixteen percent) and Second Schedule, 17th edition 2026-27 (https://pra.punjab.gov.pk/Downloads/THE-PUNJAB-SALES-TAX-ON-SERVICES-ACT-2012-17th-Edition-2026-2027.pdf)                                                                |
| Services, Sindh (SRB)                       | 13%  | to 30 June 2024       | The Sindh Finance Act 2024 (Sindh Act II of 2024) replaces "13%" with "15%" (https://www.pas.gov.pk/uploads/acts/Sindh%20Act%20No.II%20of%202024.pdf)                                                                                                                                                        |
| Services, Sindh (SRB)                       | 15%  | from 1 July 2024      | The same Act, from 1 July 2024; s. 8(1) of the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act 2011 as consolidated for 2025-26 (https://www.srb.gos.pk/srb/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Sindh-Sales-Tax-Act-2011-25-26-2.pdf)                                                                                                 |
| Services, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPRA)         | 15%  | whole period          | KP Finance Act 2019, Second Schedule, from 1 July 2019 (https://kpcode.kp.gov.pk/uploads/The_Khyber_Pakhtunkhwa_Finance_Act_2019.pdf); KP Sales Tax on Services Act 2022, s. 9(1), updated to the Finance Act 2026 (https://kpra.gov.pk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/KPSTSA-2022-Updated-Finance-act-2026.pdf) |
| Services, Balochistan (BRA)                 | 15%  | whole period          | Balochistan Sales Tax on Services Act 2015, s. 10(1) and Second Schedule, consolidated to the Finance Act 2024 (https://bra.gob.pk/NewsDirectory/2015_BSTS_Act_Ver01.pdf); BRA's FAQ (https://bra.gob.pk/FAQs.aspx)                                                                                          |
| Services, Islamabad Capital Territory (FBR) | 16%  | to 30 June 2022       | ICT (Tax on Services) Ordinance 2001, Schedule, Table 1; the Finance Act 2022 replaces "Sixteen" with "Fifteen" (https://fbr.gov.pk/Budget2022-23/FinanceAct/Finance-Act-2022.pdf)                                                                                                                           |
| Services, Islamabad Capital Territory (FBR) | 15%  | from 1 July 2022      | The same Act, from 1 July 2022; FBR's ICT Ordinance "updated up to 30.06.2025" (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/2025711172945966ICTOUpdatedupto30.06.2025.pdf)                                                                                                                                             |

How sure we are:

- **Verified** from the Act or Finance Act itself: every change of rate and
  every current rate.
- **The earlier rates (federal 17%, Sindh 13%, ICT 16%)** are confirmed as the
  rate the amending Act replaced. That they applied all the way back to
  1 July 2019 rests on finding no amendment in between, not on a 2019
  consolidation.
- **The federal rise to 18%** was first notified by S.R.O. 179(I)/2023 of
  14 February 2023, which is not on FBR's website; the dataset uses
  23 February 2023, when the Finance (Supplementary) Act 2023 took effect.
- **Balochistan for 2025-26 and 2026-27**: BRA's consolidated Act goes up to
  the Finance Act 2024, and BRA's own FAQ, which is undated, still gives 15%.
  The Balochistan Finance Acts 2025 and 2026 were not found online.
- **Islamabad Capital Territory after 30 June 2025**: FBR has not published a
  2026 consolidation; the Finance Act 2026 does not amend the ICT Ordinance.
- In Balochistan, ICT and (before 2022) Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the law has no
  single "standard rate": it is the rate on almost every line of the
  Schedule, which BRA's FAQ and FBR's circular call the standard rate.

## Income tax on salary (`income-tax-slabs.json`)

- **Dataset:** `income-tax-slabs.json` (id `income-tax-slabs`), 8 records. Tax years 2020-2027.
- **Source:** Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), Income Tax Ordinance 2001, First Schedule, Part I, Division I, clause (2), as substituted by the Finance Act 2026, s. 5(44)(a)(i) (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20266291261044366FinanceAct2026.pdf), dated 2026-06-26; retrieved 2026-11-18, checked 2026-11-18.
- **Applies:** 2019-07-01 to 2027-06-30.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-07-15 (after the Finance Act each July).

The salaried rate table for each tax year: Division I of Part I of the First
Schedule to the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, clause (2), which applies where
salary is more than 75% of taxable income. Edited directly. Each year was
read from FBR's own consolidated Ordinance for that year, and checked against
the next year's consolidation, whose footnote quotes the table it replaced.
Every band's fixed amount equals the previous band's fixed amount plus its
rate on its width (the tests check this). All documents retrieved 2026-11-18.

| Tax year       | Law                                             | Source                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| 2021 (2020-21) | Finance Act 2019, unchanged by Finance Act 2020 | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/202011414113915861I.T.OrdinanceAmendedupto(30-06-2020).pdf             |
| 2022 (2021-22) | Finance Act 2019, unchanged by Finance Act 2021 | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20217141672549772IncomeTaxOrdinanceAmendedupto30.06.2021.pdf           |
| 2023 (2022-23) | Finance Act 2022                                | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/202412215123222278IncomeTaxOrdinanceAmendedupto30.06.2022.pdf          |
| 2024 (2023-24) | Finance Act 2023                                | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/202412215122448762IncomeTaxOrdinance,2001Amendedupto30.06.2023.pdf     |
| 2025 (2024-25) | Finance Act 2024                                | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/2024751675120641IncomeTaxOrdinance,2001-amended-upto30.06.2024.pdf     |
| 2026 (2025-26) | Finance Act 2025                                | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/2025881983148210Income-Tax-Ordinance,-2001-Amended-upto-31.07.2025.pdf |
| 2027 (2026-27) | Finance Act 2026                                | Finance Act 2026 (primary) and two further sources, listed below                                         |

Tax year 2027 has three sources, all retrieved 2026-11-18:

1. **Primary: the Finance Act, 2026**, Gazette of Pakistan (Extraordinary),
   Part I, 26 June 2026
   (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20266291261044366FinanceAct2026.pdf).
   - Section 5(44)(a)(i) substitutes the table in clause (2) of Division I,
     Part I, First Schedule (Gazette page 580). Its eight bands, fixed
     amounts and rates match `income-tax-slabs.json` exactly.
   - Section 1(2) brings the Act into force on 1 July 2026, the first day of
     tax year 2027.
   - Section 5(2)(b) replaces the 9% salaried surcharge in the proviso to
     section 4AB with "no surcharge shall be payable".
   - This is the URL in the dataset's `source` field for 2027.
2. **FBR's explanation: Circular No. 02 of 2026-27 (Income Tax)**, C. No.
   1(50)S(ITP)/2026, 8 September 2026
   (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/202698139527880CircularNo.2of2026-27.pdf).
   - Paragraph 7 restates the same table.
   - Paragraph 8 confirms that the 9% surcharge on salaried individuals is
     withdrawn, while the 10% surcharge on other individuals and associations
     of persons continues.
   - The circular does not name a tax year, which is why the commencement
     comes from the Act.
3. **FBR's consolidated Ordinance**
   (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/2026724177725705IncomeTaxOrdinanace2001.pdf).
   It prints the same table, with a footnote quoting the 2026 table it
   replaced.

How sure we are, and what is left out:

- **Verified** from FBR's consolidated Ordinance for each year. For 2027 the
  table was also checked against the Finance Act, 2026 as gazetted and FBR
  Circular No. 02 of 2026-27. For earlier years the Finance Act texts
  (Gazette) were not read; FBR's consolidations are the source.
- **Not applied** (out of scope): tax credits, exemptions, the separate
  rate for pension from a former employer (2026 onwards: 0% up to Rs 10
  million, 5% above), super tax under section 4C, and withholding
  adjustments. The section 4AB surcharge is applied on request; see below.
- Tax is rounded half up to the paisa; the Ordinance's own rounding to whole
  rupees is left to the caller.

### Surcharge under section 4AB (`surcharge` in `income-tax-slabs.json`)

Since 2.7.0 each tax year carries the section 4AB surcharge, which
`calculateSalaryTax` adds with `includeSurcharge: true` (off by default in
2.x). The section's wording, the same in every version: a surcharge "at the
rate of ten percent of the income tax imposed under Division I of Part I of
the First Schedule where the taxable income exceeds rupees ten million". It
is a percentage of the whole tax from the rate table, not of the tax on the
income above Rs 10 million, so one rupee over the threshold adds it in full
(there is no marginal relief in the section). All documents retrieved
2026-11-22.

| Tax year  | Salaried rate | Law                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Source                                                                                                   |
| --------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2020–2024 | none          | Section 4AB did not exist (it is absent from FBR's consolidated Ordinance amended up to 30.06.2023)                                                                                                                                                             | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/202412215122448762IncomeTaxOrdinance,2001Amendedupto30.06.2023.pdf     |
| 2025      | 10%           | Finance Act 2024, s. 8(2), Gazette of Pakistan (Extraordinary), 30 June 2024, p. 279: inserts section 4AB; in force 1 July 2024 (s. 1(2))                                                                                                                       | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/2024630146346801FinanceAct-2024.pdf                                    |
| 2026      | 9%            | Finance Act 2025: adds the proviso "in case of an individual deriving income chargeable under the head Salary, a surcharge shall be payable at the rate of nine percent", per FBR's consolidated Ordinance amended up to 31.07.2025 (footnote 5 to section 4AB) | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/2025881983148210Income-Tax-Ordinance,-2001-Amended-upto-31.07.2025.pdf |
| 2027      | none          | Finance Act 2026, s. 5(2)(b): the proviso now reads "no surcharge shall be payable"                                                                                                                                                                             | https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20266291261044366FinanceAct2026.pdf                                    |

Supporting FBR documents:

- **Circular No. 01 of 2025-26 (Income Tax)**, C. No. 4(32) IT-Budget/2025,
  2 August 2025, page 3: the employer collects the "surcharge, if applicable
  under the provision of section 4AB, at the rate of 9%"
  (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/2025841183918948CircularNo01of2025-26IncomeTax.pdf).
- **Circular No. 02 of 2026-27 (Income Tax)**, 8 September 2026, paragraph
  8: the nine percent surcharge on salaried individuals is withdrawn, and the
  ten percent surcharge on other individuals and associations of persons
  continues (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/202698139527880CircularNo.2of2026-27.pdf).
- **FBR's consolidated Ordinance (2026)** prints section 4AB with the 2026
  proviso and footnotes for each amendment
  (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/2026724177725705IncomeTaxOrdinanace2001.pdf).

How sure we are:

- **Verified** from the section's text in each consolidation and, for 2025
  and 2027, from the Finance Act as gazetted. The Finance Act 2025 itself
  was not read: FBR's budget pages returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-22. The 9%
  rate for 2026 rests on FBR's consolidation and Circular No. 01 of 2025-26.
- **Only salaried individuals are covered**, because only the salaried rate
  table is: the 10% rate for other individuals and associations of persons
  is not applied.
- The surcharge is rounded half up to the paisa, like the tax.

## Roman Urdu name spellings (`data/sources/roman-urdu-names.json`)

Not used by the library at run time: a test list for `romanUrduKey`. It
groups everyday spellings of 118 common Pakistani given names and surnames
(277 spellings), compiled for PakDataKit's tests from common usage; it is
not an official list. In 2.7.0, 96.8% of pairs of spellings of the same name
share a key, and 8 of 38,004 pairs of different names (0.021%) do, all from
two close pairs: Sajid and Sajjad, and Amna and Amina. The test suite fails
if these rates get worse than 95% and 0.05%.

## Urdu alphabetical order (no dataset)

`compareUrdu` follows the Unicode CLDR collation tailoring for Urdu
(`common/collation/ur.xml`, "standard", CLDR release 49, unchanged since
2015), https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr/blob/release-49/common/collation/ur.xml,
retrieved 2026-11-18. Its own reference is the CRULP/PAN Localization paper
"Urdu Encoding and Collation Sequence". The government's National Language
Promotion Department (https://nlpd.gov.pk) does not publish a sort order
online, so CLDR is the order cited. The implementation was checked against
ICU's `ur` collator (Node.js, CLDR 48, identical rules) on 200,000 random
pairs of Urdu words.

## Electricity and gas bill numbers

No dataset: `parseElectricityRef` and `validateGasConsumerNumber` check the
formats that the utilities' own bill pages ask for. All pages were retrieved
on 2026-11-18.

- **DISCO reference number**: 14 digits, with urban or rural chosen
  separately (`U`/`R`), on PITC's bill pages for all 11 companies
  (https://bill.pitc.com.pk/lescobill and the same for gepco, fesco, iesco,
  mepco, pesco, hazeco, hesco, sepco, qesco and tesco). PITC's illustration
  groups it as 2 + 5 + 7 digits, which is how `formatted` shows it.
- **DISCO customer ID**: 10 digits, or 11 for LESCO (the same PITC pages).
- **K-Electric account number**: "13 digits KE Account Number starting from
  04000" (https://beta.ke.com.pk/know-your-area-status/ and
  https://ke.com.pk/bills-e-payments/). K-Electric says its contract and
  consumer numbers are for its internal use, so they are not accepted.
- **SNGPL consumer number**: 11 digits
  (https://www.sngpl.com.pk/login.jsp?mdids=85).
- **SSGC customer number**: "10-digit Customer Number"
  (https://viewbill.ssgc.com.pk/web/).
- **Not published**: what the reference number's digit groups mean, which
  digits belong to which DISCO, and any check digit. So `disco` is `null`
  except for K-Electric, and only the format is checked. IESCO also notes
  that reference numbers can change
  (https://www.iesco.com.pk/search-reference-number).

## Couriers

No dataset: `mapCourierStatus` maps only the statuses a courier documents
publicly. All pages were retrieved on 2026-11-18.

- **PostEx**: "Merchant API Integration Guide", version M- v4.1.9 (undated):
  order status IDs 1 to 9 and 15 to 18 (§3.15) and tracking history codes
  0001 to 0008 and 0013 (§3.8). The guide is PostEx's own, but it is hosted
  on Amazon S3
  (https://merchant-api-guide.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/PostEx-COD_API_Integration_Guide_V4.1.9.pdf)
  and not linked from postex.pk. Its history codes 0002, 0006 and 0007 all
  read "Returned"; "Package on Root" is mapped as written and also as "on
  route".
- **Leopards**: only "Returned to Shipper", defined in its e-commerce FAQ
  (https://ecom.leopardscourier.com/faqs). Its API documentation site
  (https://merchantapi.leopardscourier.com) has no content.
- **TCS, M&P, Trax and BlueEx**: no public status list. Their API documents
  are behind merchant or developer logins, so nothing is mapped. Copies on
  third-party sites were not used.
- **Tracking numbers**: no courier documents a format, so there is no
  tracking-number detection. PostEx's guide only uses the placeholder
  `CX-XXXXXXXXXXX`.

`normalizeCityForCourier`'s short forms (`LHR`, `Khi`, `Pindi`, `ISB`, `FSD`,
the former name Lyallpur, Urdu names and so on) are common usage, not an
official list. Each maps to a city in `cities.json`.

## FBR Digital Invoicing

- **Dataset:** `fbr-sale-types.json` (id `fbr-sale-types`), 24 records. The 24 sale types named in the specification's 28 sandbox scenarios.
- **Source:** Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), Pakistan Revenue Automation (PRAL), Technical Specification for DI API, version 1.12, section 9 'Scenarios for Sandbox Testing', column 'Sale Type' (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20257301172130815TechnicalDocumentationforDIAPIV1.12.pdf), dated 2025-07-24; retrieved 2026-11-23, checked 2026-11-23.
- **Applies:** 2025-07-24 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-02-23 (when PRAL publishes a new version of the DI technical specification; checked quarterly).

No dataset: `buildFbrInvoice` and `validateFbrInvoice` follow these
documents, retrieved on 2026-11-18:

- **PRAL, "Technical Specification for DI API", version 1.12** (issued
  7 April 2025, last updated 24 July 2025):
  https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20257301172130815TechnicalDocumentationforDIAPIV1.12.pdf,
  linked from https://www.fbr.gov.pk/di-technical-assistance/173967/173970.
  PRAL's download index (https://dicrm.pral.com.pk/assets/docs/documents.json)
  lists it as the current version. It gives the fields, the sale types and
  the error codes.
- **PRAL, "Error Message Guide (Sales)"**:
  https://dicrm.pral.com.pk/assets/docs/Manuals/Error%20Message%20Guide%20-%20(Sales).pdf.
  This is the source of the rules on numbers (0300: not negative or empty;
  0302: at most 2 decimals, 4 for quantity), on SROs (0077, 0078) and on
  reduced-rate goods (0091).
- **PRAL, "DI Scenarios Description for Sandbox Testing"** (v1.11): the sample
  invoices, used for the arithmetic examples (1000 × 18% = 180; Rs.3 × 12 =
  36; retail price 100 × 18% = 18 for Third Schedule goods).
- **Legal basis**: S.R.O. 69(I)/2025, Sales Tax Rules chapter XIV
  (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/SROs/2025129141598258SRO69(I)2025.pdf).

Where the documents disagree or are silent, the code does this:

- **Key names** are those of the specification's sample JSON
  (`invoiceType`, `buyerRegistrationType`), not the misspellings in its field
  table, and `invoiceType` is `Sale Invoice` (the table says "Sales
  Invoice", but the samples and the document type API say "Sale Invoice").
- **NTN length** is 7 (error 0002's text also mentions 9, but 0401, 0402 and
  the guide say 7 or 13).
- **Rounding**: none is documented. Sales tax is rounded half up to the
  paisa, and a declared tax within one paisa of it is accepted. This is the
  library's choice.
- **Sale types** are compared ignoring case and spaces, because the
  specification's table and its samples differ in capitals.
- **Not checked**: anything that needs FBR's reference APIs or records
  (registration, provinces, HS codes, units, rates, sale types, SRO lists,
  the original invoice of a debit note). There are no string length limits
  in the specification, so none are checked.

**Reference data (2.8.0).** `fbr-sale-types.json` lists the 24 sale types
named in the specification's sandbox scenarios (section 9), with the
scenarios that use each (`getSaleTypes()`). The specification shows only
sample rows of FBR's other reference lists (2 provinces, 2 units, 3
transaction types), and the full lists come from PRAL's reference APIs
(`/pdi/v1/provinces`, `/pdi/v1/uom`, `/pdi/v2/HS_UOM`,
`/pdi/v2/SaleTypeToRate` …), which need the taxpayer's token. FBR publishes
no other HS code-to-unit list for sales tax: the only official PCT-to-unit
list found is a customs order (Customs General Order 5 of 2022, Annex-I,
7,575 codes, no descriptions), which is not shipped as Digital Invoicing
reference data. So `validateFbrInvoice(invoice, { reference })` checks
provinces, sale types, units and HS code/unit pairs against the lists an
app syncs from FBR's APIs, which are authoritative; without them those
values are checked for presence only.

## CNIC

First digit = province of registration, per FBR's tax-ID description filed with
the OECD (1 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 2 former FATA, 3 Punjab, 4 Sindh, 5
Balochistan, 6 Islamabad, 7 Gilgit-Baltistan). `8` for Azad Jammu and Kashmir
comes from secondary sources only. Last digit odd = male, even = female.

## Passport numbers

`validatePassport` accepts two letters followed by seven digits (`AB1234567`).
DGIP does not publish the format, and its forms only ask for "Passport Number".

- **Source:** the EU Council's PRADO register gives this pattern for the 2013
  ordinary passport
  (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/prado/en/PAK-AO-02003/index.html). The page
  sits behind a bot check, so it was confirmed through search-result text, not
  the page itself.
- **Observed on real passports:** the maintainer checked real ordinary
  (green) and official (blue) Pakistani passports in November 2026; their
  numbers have this shape. No numbers are recorded here.
- **Fits ICAO Doc 9303:** the document-number field is 9 characters, with the
  check digit stored separately in the machine-readable zone
  (https://www.icao.int/publications/Documents/9303_p4_cons_en.pdf).
- **Still unconfirmed:** diplomatic (red) passports and the e-passport
  variants (2022 onwards), and what the letters mean. A real number in another
  shape will be rejected; treat `false` as unusual, not fake.

## Vehicle registration plates

`parseVehiclePlate` accepts 1–4 letters, then 1–4 digits, optionally followed
by a two-digit year after a separator (`LEA-1234-19`). There is no national
format: each province's excise department sets its own.

- **Reported formats** (Wikipedia, partly inconsistent,
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_registration_plates_of_Pakistan):
  Sindh cars 3 letters + 3 digits; Islamabad and Balochistan 2 letters + 3
  digits; Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 2 letters + 4 digits; Gilgit-Baltistan 3 letters +
  2 digits; AJK motorcycles and public transport 4 letters + 3 digits; older
  Punjab plates 4 digits plus a two-digit year.
- **Number length:** Punjab's excise department auctions registration marks of
  1 to 4 digits (https://excise.punjab.gov.pk/auctions).
- **Recent changes:** numbers now stay with the owner in Islamabad
  (https://profit.pakistantoday.com.pk/2025/07/20/ict-excise-deptt-introduces-personalized-number-plates-digital-cards-online-tax-payment/),
  Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
  (https://arynews.tv/kp-new-vehicle-registration-number-plate-system-sep-17-2025)
  and Sindh, from 16 February 2026
  (https://profit.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/02/16/sindh-enforces-cnic-based-number-plates-owners-can-retain-registration-marks/).
  Punjab announced new series from May 2026
  (https://propakistani.pk/2026/04/29/punjab-to-launch-five-new-vehicle-number-series/)
  without publishing their layout.
- **Not checked:** series letters against districts (no official list, e.g. for
  `LEA`/`LEB` = Lahore), and labels printed on the plate such as "ICT" or
  "PUNJAB", which are not part of the number.

## Zakat nisab (`zakat-nisab.json`)

- **Dataset:** `zakat-nisab.json` (id `zakat-nisab`), 15 records. Zakat years 1433-1447 AH (1432-33 to 1446-47 in the notifications; 2012-2026).
- **Source:** Ministry of Poverty Alleviation & Social Safety (Administrator-General Zakat); State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), Notification No. CE-1001(36)/NISAB/1446-47/2026-48, conveyed by SBP BPRD Circular Letter No. 03 of 2026; each year has its own notification and circular (https://www.sbp.org.pk/bprd/2026/CL3-Notification.pdf), dated 2026-02-16; retrieved 2026-11-23, checked 2026-11-23.
- **Applies:** 2012-07-21 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-02-15 (each year shortly before 1 Ramazan, when the Ministry notifies the next nisab and SBP circulates it).

The nisab for compulsory Zakat deduction at source from savings, profit and
loss sharing and similar accounts (asset code 101), for each Zakat year from
1433 AH (2012) to 1447 AH (2026). Each record comes from two documents,
retrieved 2026-11-23:

- the Ministry of Poverty Alleviation & Social Safety's notification of the
  nisab fixed by the Administrator-General Zakat, which states it in
  figures and in words (they agree in every year); and
- the SBP BPRD circular letter that sends it to banks, with SBP's bank
  holiday circular for the deduction day where there is one.

SBP's www site blocks automated downloads, so the files were read from
SBP's own mirror, `archive.sbp.org.pk`, at the same paths. The scanned
notifications (2012-2024) were read from the page images.

**Rules** (Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980 and the Zakat (Collection and
Refund) Rules 1981, from pakistancode.gov.pk and pass.gov.pk):

- **Rate:** 2.5% of the balance at the start of the valuation date (First
  Schedule, S. No. 1).
- **Accounts:** the nisab applies to savings and similar accounts (asset
  code 101). Current accounts and foreign currency accounts are not subject
  to compulsory deduction (Second Schedule, S. No. 4).
- **Exemption:** a holder who files the declaration on Form CZ-50 at least
  30 days before the valuation date is not deducted (s. 1(3), proviso (a);
  rule 20).

**Rounding:** Zakat is rounded to the nearest rupee, as the First
Schedule's Note 2 says: an amount under a rupee is not charged; otherwise 50
paisa or more counts as a rupee and less than 50 paisa is dropped.

**Exemption:** the declaration (Form CZ-50) must be filed with the bank at
least 30 days before the valuation date, sworn before a magistrate, oath
commissioner, notary public or other person authorised to administer
oaths, in the presence of two witnesses (s. 1(3), proviso (a)). The library
takes `exempt: true` to mean such a declaration is on file; it does not
check it.

**Conventions and limits:**

- `zakatYear` is the Hijri year of the valuation date, 1 Ramazan (`1447` is
  February 2026); the notification calls the same deduction "1446-47"
  (`label`). The Ordinance says a Zakat year starts on 1 Ramazan, which
  would name it 1447-48.
- **Valuation date (`ramazan1`):** 1 Ramazan as the Central
  Ruet-e-Hilal Committee announced it, with the outlet that reported the
  announcement (`ramazan1Source`); dates are assigned to Zakat years by it.
  The notifications only say 1 Ramazan is "likely to fall on" one of two
  days; that text is kept as a quoted `note`.
- **Deduction day (`bankHolidayDate`):** the bank holiday SBP declares for
  the deduction. It is 1 Ramazan, or the next working day when 1 Ramazan is
  a weekend or public holiday: 1433 (SBP BPRD Circular Letter No. 17 of
  2012: 1 Ramzan on Saturday or Sunday, so Monday 23 July 2012), 1438,
  1441, 1443, 1446, and 1444 (1 Ramazan was Pakistan Day, 23 March 2023, so
  24 March). `null` for 1434 and 1435, where no holiday circular was found.
- **Boundary:** a balance equal to the nisab is deducted. Every
  notification from 1433 to 1447 says no deduction where the balance is
  "less than" the nisab (2026: deduction on "Rs. 503,529/- or above"), and
  s. 2(xxiii) defines a sahib-e-nisab as a person who owns assets "not less
  than nisab". The First Schedule, S. No. 1, as printed by Pakistan Code,
  says no deduction where the balance "does not exceed" the nisab, which
  would not deduct it.
- **Provinces:** in Punjab the Punjab Zakat and Ushr Act 2018 (s. 27(1))
  repealed the 1980 Ordinance; its First Schedule uses the same "does not
  exceed" wording, with the nisab "as notified by the Chief Administrator
  Zakat"
  (https://punjabcode.punjab.gov.pk/uploads/articles/the-punjab-zakat-and-ushr-act-2018-pdf.pdf).
- **Not covered:** years before 1433 AH (no nisab circular in SBP's indexes
  for 2005-2011) and any later amendment to the 1981 Rules or Form CZ-50
  (the Rules were read in their 1989 consolidation).
- Document quirks: the 1433 notification itself reads "No. CE-1001(36)/NISAB/1432-33/2012" (checked on the scanned letter), and SBP's circular quotes it as
  "CE-100(36)"; the 1436 number ends "/2015/" with the serial blank in
  the original, and SBP BPRD Circular Letter No. 14 of 2015 prints it the
  same way; the 1442 notification, dated April 2021, prints the deduction
  month as "April, 2020".

## Population (`district-population.json`, `tehsil-population.json`)

- **Dataset:** `district-population.json` (id `district-population`), 177 records. All 177 current districts; figures for the 133 that existed at the census in the four provinces and Islamabad.
- **Source:** Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Table 1 'Area, population by sex, sex ratio, population density, urban proportion, household size and annual growth rate' and Table 20 'Type of housing unit by region', by district (https://www.pbs.gov.pk/result-excel/), dated 2025-08-25; retrieved 2026-11-23, checked 2026-11-23.
- **Applies:** 2023-03-01 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-11-23 (fixed census results; checked yearly for PBS corrections, and districts are relinked when one is created).
- **Dataset:** `tehsil-population.json` (id `tehsil-population`), 591 records. All 591 tehsil-level units of the census, with their census and current district.
- **Source:** Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, Tables 1 and 20, by tehsil, taluka and sub-division (https://www.pbs.gov.pk/result-excel/), dated 2025-08-25; retrieved 2026-11-23, checked 2026-11-23.
- **Applies:** 2023-03-01 to now.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-11-23 (fixed census results; checked yearly for PBS corrections, and districts are relinked when one is created).

Population, households and the urban/rural split from the 7th Population and
Housing Census 2023 (Pakistan Bureau of Statistics), from PBS's detailed
results in Excel (https://www.pbs.gov.pk/result-excel/, published 25 August
2025, retrieved 2026-11-23):

- **Population, urban and rural:** Table 1, "Area, population by sex, sex
  ratio, population density, urban proportion, household size and annual
  growth rate", the "all sexes" figure on each unit's total, urban and rural
  rows (`table_1_<province>_districts.xlsx`).
- **Households:** Table 20, "Type of housing unit by region", the households
  column on the "all localities" row (`table_20_<province>_districts.xlsx`).
  Its national total, 38,292,556, is the census report's headline count.
  PBS does not define the column further.

The figures were checked three ways: every district's urban and rural
figures add up to its total; each district's tehsils add up to the
district; and the districts of each province add up to PBS's provincial
totals (Punjab 127,688,922, Sindh 55,696,147, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
40,856,097, Balochistan 14,894,402, Islamabad 2,363,863). All 136 census
districts also match PBS's PDF edition of Table 1.

How districts are linked:

- **133 districts** match a census district. Names were matched by letter
  case and spacing, plus these aliases: Kolai-Palas (Kolai Palas Kohistan),
  Tor Ghar (Torghar), Sheerani (Sherani), Qambar Shahdadkot (Kambar Shahdad
  Kot), Malakand (Malakand District).
- **20 districts created after the census** have `null` figures. Each names
  the census district its area was part of (`censusDistrict`), from the
  district notes above; the figures are not estimated or split.
- **14 districts that lost area** to a new district (Rawalpindi, Chakwal,
  Gujranwala, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Swat, Upper Dir, Batagram,
  Dera Ismail Khan, Lasbela, Jaffarabad, Pishin, Kech and Khuzdar) keep the
  census figures for their census boundary, with `boundaryChanged: true`.
  For today's boundary, add up the tehsils with `getTehsilPopulation`.
- **Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir** (24 districts) were not
  enumerated by this census, so their figures are `null`.

Errors in PBS's files, corrected:

- Table 1 drops the letters "ALL" from some names in both the Excel and PDF
  editions ("TANDO AHYAR", "AI", "KAR KAHAR", "KAR SAYADDAN"); the names come
  from Table 20, whose rows are in the same order.
- Topi tehsil's rural figure in the Excel edition repeats its total; the PDF
  edition's 307,695 is used.
- The Panjgur sub-tehsil this dataset (and Table 1) calls "Kag" is printed
  "KALLAG" in Table 20, at the same position and with the same household
  size; the name is kept as in Table 1 and is unverified.

## Withholding tax rates (`withholding-rates.json`)

- **Dataset:** `withholding-rates.json` (id `withholding-rates`), 98 records. Tax years 2025-2027: sections 149, 150, 151, 153, 154B (2027), 231AB, 236C and 236K.
- **Source:** Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), Withholding Income Tax Rate Card, tax year 2027, updated up to 30 June 2026 as per Finance Act 2026; checked against the Income Tax Ordinance 2001 as amended by Finance Act 2026. Each tax year has its own card. (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/202681113864992WithholdingTaxRatesCard2027.pdf), dated 2026-08-11; retrieved 2026-11-23, checked 2026-11-23.
- **Applies:** 2024-07-01 to 2027-06-30.
- **Next expected update:** 2027-08-15 (after the Finance Act each July, when FBR publishes the next tax year's rate card).

Rates for persons on and not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List (ATL), for
sections 149 (salary), 150 (dividends), 151 (profit on debt), 153 (goods,
services and contracts), 154B (social media income, from tax year 2027),
231AB (cash withdrawal), 236C (sale of immovable property) and 236K
(purchase of immovable property). One record per section, case and tax
year, each with the card's own references.

Sources, all from FBR's rate card page
(https://fbr.gov.pk/withholding-taxes-rate-card/174298/174301), retrieved
2026-11-23. The cards print no date; the dates are the PDFs' creation dates.

- **Tax year 2027:** "Updated up to June 30, 2026 as per Finance Act,
  2026", PDF dated 2026-08-11, also read in FBR's xlsx edition
  (https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/202681113864992WithholdingTaxRatesCard2027.pdf).
- **Tax year 2026:** "Updated up to June 30, 2025 as per Finance Act,
  2025", PDF dated 2025-08-15, also read in FBR's xlsx edition
  (http://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20258181281745641WHT-RateCard.pdf).
- **Tax year 2025:** "Withholding Income Tax Regime (WHT Rates Card) ...
  updated up to June 30, 2024", PDF dated 2024-08-21; a scan, read from the
  page images and FBR's docx edition
  (http://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20248211184455183WithholdingTaxRegimeRatesCard2024.pdf).

Every row was then checked against FBR's consolidated Income Tax Ordinance
2001 for its year: amended up to 30.06.2024 (tax year 2025), 31.07.2025
(2026) and 30 June 2026 (2027), with the Finance Act 2026
(https://download1.fbr.gov.pk/Docs/20266291261044366FinanceAct2026.pdf).
Of 124 card rows, 121 match. The card says the Ordinance prevails, so:

- **153(2), services to exporters, tax year 2027:** the card shows 1%
  (non-ATL 2%), but Finance Act 2026, s. 5(44)(b)(v)(B), substitutes 1.25%
  in Division IV, para (3), Part III of the First Schedule. The dataset uses
  1.25% (non-ATL 2.5%) and says so in `statuteOverride`.
- **150, "mutual funds deriving fifty percent or more income from profit
  on debt", 25%, tax years 2026 and 2027:** Finance Act 2025 replaced
  clause (b) without that proviso and inserted clause (ba) ("25% and 15%"
  by the fund's income from profit on debt). The row is left out for 2026
  and 2027 and kept for 2025, when it applied.

- **150, clause (ba), a company receiving the dividend (2026, 2027):** the
  proviso taxes the part derived from debt securities at 29% (FBR's
  Ordinance amended up to 31.07.2025 and up to 30 June 2026). No card shows
  it. It is its own case, `mutual-fund-debt-part-company`, at 29% (58% for a
  company not on the ATL: Tenth Schedule R.1; section 150 is not excluded
  by R.10).

The 153(2) citation was checked against the enacted Finance Act 2026
(Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 26 June 2026, pp. 583-584),
where the Income Tax Ordinance amendments are section 5; the Finance Bill
numbered them section 6.

**The non-ATL rule is each case's own** (Tenth Schedule), not one
multiplier:

- **Doubled** (R.1, "increased by hundred percent"): 150, 151 (2026,
  2027), 153 and 154B.
- **A fixed rate** (R.1, table): 236C (10% in 2025, 11.5% in 2026 and 2027) and 151 (35% in 2025).
- **Its own value bands** (R.1, proviso): 236K (12/16/20% in 2025,
  10.5/14.5/18.5% in 2026 and 2027).
- **Only for persons not on the ATL:** 231AB (excluded from R.1 by
  R.10(ga)); 0.6% in 2025, 0.8% in 2026 and 2027.
- **None:** 149 (excluded by R.10(a)); the salaried rate table applies to
  everyone.
- **Late filers** (R.1A, 2025 and 2026 only; omitted by Finance Act 2026):
  236C and 236K have their own value bands.

**Thresholds (settled):** 231AB is on the day's aggregate cash
withdrawals. Once it exceeds Rs 50,000, the tax is on the whole sum; Rs
50,000 itself is not taxed. The threshold is in the section's text in all
three years, though no card shows it. 236C and 236K bands are chosen by the
whole gross consideration or fair market value, not applied in slices:
up to Rs 50 million, up to Rs 100 million, and above. Rs 50 million and Rs
100 million fall in the lower band (FBR's wording is "does not exceed").

**Rounding:** the tax is rounded to the nearest rupee, as section 219 of
the Ordinance requires for "any amount of tax or refund payable under this
Ordinance" (under 50 paisa dropped, 50 paisa or more counted as a rupee).
It is computed exactly and rounded once.

**Sukuk (151, individual or AOP):** the statute gives 12.5% where the
return on investment is "more than one million" and 10% where it is "less
than one million". A return of exactly Rs 1 million is in neither, so the
library returns no rate for it, and a case that does not fit the return
(`returnOnInvestment`, default the amount) is rejected.

**154B (settled):** 5% for persons on the ATL and 10% for persons not on
it, residents and non-residents alike (TY2027 card; Tenth Schedule R.10
does not exclude 154B). Section 154B(3) makes it a minimum tax for a
resident and a final tax for a non-resident without a permanent
establishment in Pakistan.

**FBR's explanation:** Circular No. 02 of 2026-27 (8 September 2026)
confirms the 2027 service rates (paragraph 22: 7%, 15%, 12% and 14%) and
the 1.25% export rate (paragraph 30); those records cite it in `circular`.

**153(2A):** the e-commerce cases name section 153(2A) in their law
reference.

Other notes: the 2025 card cites Division X for 236K, where the statute
has Division XVIII; the cards say "Independent Power Purchasers" where the
statute says "Producers"; clause (ba)'s 29% rate on the debt part of a
dividend received by a company is in the statute but not on the card, and
is not applied.

Not covered: every other section of the card (for example 152, 155, 156,
231B, 234, 235, 236, 236G, 236H, 236Y), exemptions, reduced-rate
certificates, and whether a deduction is adjustable, minimum or final.
